pages.title: File:Willis Street Power Station, Willis Street, Cass Park, Midtown, Detroit, MI - 54219934210.jpg

ObjectName.value: Willis Street Power Station, Willis Street, Cass Park, Midtown, Detroit, MI - 54219934210

Categories.value: Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|2024 in Detroit|Willis Avenue Station

ImageDescription.value: Built in 1903-1904 and significantly expanded between 1916 and 1927, this Classical Revival-style building was built for the Detroit Edison Company to serve as a steam electric power station for the city of Detroit.  The building is clad in red brick with limestone trim, three metal smokestacks on the roof, decorative patterned brickwork, doric pilasters, rusticated brickwork at the base, and metal-frame windows.  The building is a contributing structure in the Willis–Selden Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1997.  Today, the building serves as a cogeneration plant that provides power for heating and cooling for adjacent institutions and large commercial buildings, run by the Detroit Thermal Company.
